task_family: iid tabular regression (bounded continuous target on a 0.01 grid; 8 categorical/boolean features, 3 low-cardinality discrete integers, 1 near-continuous feature)

target_profile.grid: every value lies exactly on a 0.01 grid (verified)

schema_profile.note: excluding curvature the feature space is a discrete grid of 3*3*3*3*2*2*2*2*4*5*8 = 51840 cells; 2.081% of train rows are exact duplicates on the 12-feature tuple and 4.14% of test rows carry a feature tuple that also occurs in train

test_window.evidence: No date, timestamp or sequence column exists (time_of_day is a 3-level categorical, not a time index). Train and test id blocks are contiguous and disjoint (train 0-517753, test 517754-690338), a Playground synthetic-generation artifact rather than a temporal ordering. Column sets are identical apart from the target and sample_submission.csv is filled with the train-target mean (0.352), the iid-split convention. Confidence high, not proven from the description alone.
test_window.must_verify_in_stage1: per-feature train-vs-test marginals plus an adversarial-validation AUC; an AUC materially above 0.5 refutes the iid assumption

split_policy.forbidden: nothing is forbidden on temporal or group grounds — there is no date column and no entity/group key, so the TASK-TS-FUTURE time-split mandate does not fire
split_policy.caveat: 2.081% of train rows are feature-tuple duplicates, so identical feature rows can straddle folds. Over 517K rows on a ~51840-cell discrete grid that is a property of the generating process, not row-level leakage; shuffled KFold stays correct.
split_policy.reuse_note: config.yaml records a Feb-2026 run at CV RMSE 0.056074 / Public LB 0.05558 / Private 0.05583 under exactly this scheme. KFold depends only on n_samples + seed, so reusing the seed keeps July scores directly comparable.

metric.name: RMSE
traps: L2 wants the conditional mean — do NOT snap predictions onto the 0.01 target grid even though the target sits on one; the s3e14 snap-to-grid prior was tested and REJECTED on this competition (config.yaml)
target is bounded [0, 1]; unbounded regressors emit out-of-range values, so clipping is free and safe

target std is only 0.166, so score differences live in the 4th-5th decimal — take blend weights from the NNLS closed form, not a Dirichlet/random search whose ~1e-5 approximation error can exceed the real gain
517K rows make the CV standard error small, but report fold-to-fold spread alongside the mean before accepting a sub-1e-4 improvement

external_data.reasoning: Synthetic road-accident risk score with no country, region, date, currency or geography column. No whitelisted source (World Bank, holiday calendars, ISO country tables, ECB FX, OWID COVID) has a join key present in or derivable from the official data. `holiday` and `school_season` are already-resolved booleans, not dates, so a holiday-calendar join is impossible as well as redundant.
external_data.rules_status: config.yaml sets external_data_allowed: true, but no whitelisted source is joinable, so the permission is moot

injection_ideas.rationale: No date column and no group key, so the time-split mandate does not apply and shuffled KFold is admissible. Binding on the evaluator with seed 42 so July scores stay comparable to the Feb-2026 record (CV RMSE 0.056074).
injection_ideas.source_prior: TASK-TS-FUTURE (negative match — trigger absent, so its shuffled-KFold prohibition does not fire here); config.yaml Feb-2026 fold-reuse protocol

injection_ideas.rationale: Target is bounded [0, 1]; clipping inside the metric function means every CV fold and every blend candidate is scored on the same post-processed vector. round_to_int stays false deliberately: the target sits on a 0.01 grid but squared error is minimised by the conditional mean, and the snap-to-grid prior was already REJECTED on this competition.
injection_ideas.source_prior: TASK-MAE-METRIC (its postprocessing-inside-the-metric rule transfers; its L1-objective action does NOT — metric is RMSE); s3e14 snap-to-grid prior, rejected here per config.yaml

matched_task_priors_detail.why: 8 of 12 feature columns are categorical/boolean and 3 more are low-cardinality discrete integers, so encoding choice dominates. But all cardinalities are tiny (2-8) — there is no high-cardinality column, which is the part of the prior that most motivates CV-safe target encoding. The action that transfers cleanly is native GBDT categorical handling.

Trigger is a property of the blend pool, not of the data, so it fires at the blend stage. Flagged now because the prior's own evidence cites this competition's NNLS diagnostic and because the planned pool (LGB/XGB/LGBM_v2 from the Feb run) is variance-dominated and library-homogeneous — exactly the configuration the decorrelator addresses.

Metric is RMSE, an L2-family metric, so the prior's L1-objective action does NOT transfer. Only its second half — put post-processing inside the metric function so every blend candidate sees it — applies, and that is what the postprocess operator encodes.

unmatched_task_priors_checked: TASK-TS-FUTURE — no date column, no forecasting framing
TASK-TS-CALENDAR — no daily series, no store/product keys
TASK-SPECTRAL — 12 columns over 517K rows, the opposite regime
TASK-STRUCT-OUT — single scalar output, no generative grid/sequence structure
not_recorded: CV-safe target/mean encoding over the discrete categorical tuple and over 2-3 way category groups (~51840 cells, ~10 rows/cell, so group means are well-estimated and near-Bayes for the discrete part) — no operator in knowledge/injection_operators.md expresses an internal-data encoding; join_feature and flag_feature both require a whitelisted external source
binned curvature crossed with speed_limit and road_type as an encoding key — same reason: the vocabulary has no internal feature-construction operator
count/frequency encoding of the feature tuple as a confidence weight for encoded means — same reason
native GBDT categorical handling (LightGBM categorical_feature / CatBoost) instead of one-hot, the TASK-CAT-ONLY action — a model hyperparameter, and the vocabulary has no model-config operator
add one shallow heavily-regularized different-library member as a blend decorrelator, then re-optimize weights (TASK-BLEND-DECOR) — blend-pool composition is outside the operator set
take blend weights from the NNLS closed form rather than a random/Dirichlet weight search — blend-solver choice is outside the operator set
an MLP or an explicit per-cell group-mean lookup model as a genuinely different inductive bias on a small discrete grid — model-family choice is outside the operator set

explicit hand-written product/ratio interaction columns are DE-PRIORITISED (the s3e9 'explicit product interactions add nothing for GBDT' prior was CONFIRMED here: 12 base features beat the 27-feature set on solo LGB) — a negative finding, and no operator expresses it either way
official competition rules text — only the special_rules flags in config.yaml were read, the rules page was not fetched (moot: no whitelisted external source is joinable)
whether the train/test split is truly iid — asserted from schema evidence only; Stage 1 EDA must confirm via train-vs-test marginals and adversarial validation
